```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A names a concrete, reachable payer: owner-operator contractors who write their own estimates. B leaves the buyer unresolved. Its own open questions ask whether the purchaser is a non-engineer builder or an IT/security gatekeeper, which would mean a different customer and a different sales motion. That ambiguity is costly when the goal is a paying customer within 90 days.",
    "Willingness to pay is better evidenced in A. At least four competitors publish paid tiers in the $30–$125/mo range: EstimationPro, Outdoor Estimates, QuoteIQ, and CostSnap's paid tiers. In B, only display.dev and Volly show prices, and Volly's Team plan is still beta. Orb has no paid tier, 9pm is invite-only with no pricing, and Perch's price is undisclosed.",
    "A's sourced demand quote is first-hand and quantified: '1-2 hours per night' writing quotes, with a Reddit URL. B's independent demand evidence is a Reddit post about difficulty sharing tools with coworkers. It does not show anyone paying a recurring hosting fee, and B's own case against says free workarounds remain available.",
    "B carries a severe solo-operator liability in sandboxed execution of arbitrary agent code. A competitor's own README discloses a sandbox escape. A's main technical risk, estimate accuracy, is real but less catastrophic. A's riskiest feature, crew scheduling, can be deferred, and its open questions already suggest shipping quoting alone.",
    "B has cheaper sourced acquisition channels: Product Hunt at ~$3–5 CPA, plus Hacker News and free marketplace listings. This is B's strongest advantage over A's expensive paid channels. Launch-day traffic does not resolve B's unclear buyer or its thin evidence of payment, so it does not outweigh A's clearer payer and pricing evidence."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's strongest demand quote is a vendor-curated testimonial on Volly's own marketing site. The brief itself flags it as not independently verified. It comes from an interested party and cannot count as independent demand. That leaves B with only a Reddit post showing difficulty sharing tools, not intent to pay.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both ideas are crowded markets with no clear wedge, so neither is a strong first bet. A's evidence has its own gaps. Its second demand quote has no retrieved URL and counts as missing. The $237 CPL figure is a generic B2B SaaS benchmark, not specific to contractors. The claim that EstimationPro and Outdoor Estimates are run by single contractor-founders appears only in the case for, with no source. Pricing for CostSnap, Roooster, QuotrPro, and Setell is unpublished. A wins mainly because its payer and price evidence are more concrete, and its execution risk is lower than B's."
}
```
